title: Python + TS live integration workshop — auth & env quickstart
summary: AE + SE walked Brightlane through Redwood SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, focusing on auth (API keys, SSO hints), environment setup (VPC nuances, container secrets), and a short live run of the sample app. Customer raised questions around private deployment, KMS integration, and token cost tradeoffs; agreed to pilot benchmarks and share security docs.
topics: SDK install and auth patterns (api key vs SSO)
Environment variables, container secrets, CI/CD patterns
Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private for PHI workloads
Next steps: pilot benchmark, security pack, pricing
next_steps: Redwood to send tailored security pack + SOC2/ISO summary (Alyssa)
Redwood SE to provision 2-hour pilot window on Dedicated staging and share benchmark sheet (Marcus)
Customer to provide representative prompt set and dev creds to run initial latency/cost test (Kara)
Schedule follow-up deep-dive on VPC/private on-prem options w/ infra (Tomás + Marcus)
Confirm pilot timeline: target week of 2025-05-26
action_items: Alyssa: Email SOC2 summary, security questionnaire answers (due: 2025-05-16)
Marcus: Stand up Dedicated pilot instance; invite Brightlane to demo run + share benchmark spreadsheet (due: 2025-05-22)
Kara: Upload 3 canonical prompt flows and expected SLAs to shared drive (due: 2025-05-19)
Priya: Provide list of internal compliance contacts and KMS requirements (due: 2025-05-18)
transcript:
Header: 2025-05-14 16:00 PT | Duration ~60m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Kara Jensen (Brightlane EM), Tomás Rivera (Brightlane Platform Lead), Priya Nair (Brightlane DevOps)
Shared: deck - https://redwood.ai/decks/sdk-quickstart , pilot spreadsheet - (will be shared after)

[00:00] Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alyssa, AE on the account. Marcus is our SE who will run the live integration. Quick agenda — auth patterns, quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, a short live run, and then Q&A. Is that okay?
[00:32] Kara: Yep, sounds good. We mostly want to know how fast we can get a dev flow up and how it behaves inside our VPC. Also want to check on PHI handling and KMS.
[01:05] Marcus: Great. I'll start with the SDK install. We assume node 18+ for TS and Python 3.10+. Install command for Python is pip install redwood-inference, for TS npm i @redwood/inference. We'll show env var patterns for both.
[01:40] Priya: Quick question — we use HashiVault for secrets in prod. How would the API key get rotated?
[02:02] Marcus: Good q. Typical pattern: store Redwood API key as a secret in Vault and inject into container as env var at runtime. We recommend short lived keys for Dedicated; for Private you can integrate with your KMS or HSM via our connector. Small caveat: if you plan to run in an air-gapped on-prem instance, rotation flows may be slightly more manual, but we support programmatic API key rotation.
[02:45] Tomás: When you say Private, do you mean you ship a control plane into our VPC? We have strict egress policies.
[03:01] Alyssa: For Private we provide a customer-controlled control plane option — yes, it can live in your VPC and you can disable outbound egress except to the necessary infra endpoints. We'll follow up with the architecture diagram.
[03:30] Marcus: Ok demo time. Opening a simple Python quickstart. Code snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) — then client.generate(...).
[04:02] [Marcus shares screen — terminal visible] Marcus: I'm going to run the sample which calls the hosted API. Note the SDK supports streaming and function-calling style outputs; the TS SDK is nearly identical.
[04:35] [04:35] Customer: minor cross talk, lag reported.
[05:00] Marcus: We have optional debug mode that prints request/response timing. Running now... Response returned in ~120ms for a short prompt on our hosted small model.
[05:30] Priya: That's the hosted one — how would latency look on Dedicated within our cloud region?
[05:48] Marcus: On Dedicated we're colocated in the same region as your VPC — typical p95 for similar prompts we've seen is 200-350ms depending on sequence length and whether KV cache hits. We'll also include profiling hooks so you can see per-token timing.
[06:20] Kara: Can you explain KV cache briefly? Tomás wasn't familiar.
[06:34] Marcus: Sure — KV cache is the key-value cache for transformer attention states. If you have repeated prefixes it's reused and that avoids re-computation. It gives great cost reductions for chatty flows. There's also a prefix cache we can share.
[06:58] Tomás: Any mis-transcription: you said 'K-V cash' earlier but we know it's KV cache.
[07:12] Marcus: Yeah, sorry.
[07:30] [07:30] Marcus: Now the TS example: import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); client.chat.create({ messages: [...] }) — running live.
[08:05] [08:05] output: streaming JSON chunks — small glitches in the transcript where function names appear split.
[08:30] Priya: About authentication — do you support SSO for team management? We use Okta.
[08:48] Alyssa: Yes we support SAML/SSO provisioning for console access and RBAC. For API usage we still provision service keys per team or project; those can be tied to a user or service account in SSO. You can also enforce IP allowlists for keys.
[09:22] Kara: On compliance — SOC2, ISO, audit logs — we need an evidence pack for procurement.
[09:38] Alyssa: We'll send the security pack and SOC2 summary. Marcus will include specifics on logging retention and audit hooks.
[10:00] Marcus: Quick aside on cost controls: we recommend a combination of batching, prefix caching, and quantized model variants for throughput tests. In Optimize we give recommendations based on your workload profile.
[10:33] Tomás: If we quantize aggressively will quality degrade for some of our diagnostic prompts? We have edge cases.
[10:49] Marcus: There is a trade-off. Quantization tends to be model- and prompt-dependent. In the pilot we'll test a few quant profiles and measure output divergence. We'll flag any regressions in the eval harness.
[11:20] [11:20] Alyssa: Can we talk about a simple pilot plan? We're proposing a 2-week pilot on Dedicated staging, with 48-hour benchmark window and your prompts. Marcus can run the tests and produce scorecards.
[11:42] Kara: That timeline works for us as long as the initial run covers PHI masking and we get KMS integration notes.
[12:01] Marcus: For KMS, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS and HSM connectors for Private. If you need Bring Your Own Key for at-rest model checkpoints, we'll surface those options.
[12:30] Priya: Any additional network requirements? We have strict egress.
[12:45] Marcus: For Dedicated you can peer via private link or VPC peering; for Private we can deploy inline. We'll follow up with the network diagram and port list.
[13:10] [13:10] Marcus shares a tiny notebook showing the benchmark CSV columns: prompt_id, token_count, latency_ms_p50/p95, cost_usd. He runs a sample with a medium-length prompt.
[13:45] Marcus: That sample completed in about 320ms p95 and cost ~0.003 USD per request for the sample model; your cost will vary with model choice and sequence lengths.
[14:05] Tomás: Can you limit per-route quotas and per-token budgets? We need to enforce spending limits in prod.
[14:22] Alyssa: Yes per-route rate limits and soft/hard quotas are configurable in the Console; you can also set alerts for spend thresholds.
[14:50] Kara: On SDK side, is there native retry/backoff and idempotency handling?
[15:05] Marcus: Yes, SDK has retry with exponential backoff and idempotency tokens for mutating ops. We also provide client-side tracing hooks for OpenTelemetry.
[15:40] Priya: We use Kubernetes with sealed-secrets. Any guidance on deploying the SDK inside a microservice?
[15:56] Marcus: Deploy the SDK in the app container, mount the API key from sealed-secrets as env var. For high-throughput services, use a local proxy or connection pooling pattern we document in the guide. We'll share a k8s manifest example.
[16:30] [16:30] Marcus: Quick live test switching from hosted to Dedicated — toggling endpoint in env var and re-running CLI. This demonstrates minimal code change.
[17:05] Marcus: Ok now Q&A. Kara: What are typical failure modes?
[17:25] Marcus: Network blips, model OOMs if sequence length spikes, and tokenization mismatches. We have safeguards: automatic fallbacks to smaller models, rate limiting, and robust error codes.
[17:55] Tomás: For logging — can we ship raw prompts to our SIEM or do you redact by default?
[18:10] Alyssa: By default we retain metadata and flattened request logs; for PHI you can set data retention to zero and enable customer-side redaction. We can also set up a log forwarder to your SIEM.
[18:40] Priya: What about deployment automation? We want CI secrets rotation to not cause downtime.
[18:55] Marcus: Use short-lived keys and an automated rotation job tied to your CI; the SDK handles re-auth without restarting the process if keys are refreshed in env. We'll include an example GitHub Actions snippet.
[19:30] Kara: Any limitations for multi-tenant apps? We tenant by customer id.
[19:45] Marcus: We recommend scoping keys per-tenant and applying per-key quotas. Also annotate logs with tenant metadata.
[20:05] [20:05] Alyssa: Ok quick recap and next steps — we'll send the SOC2 pack, Marcus will provision Dedicated pilot, customer shares prompt set, and we'll reconvene after the benchmark window.
[20:40] Kara: Sounds good. One small concern: pricing for a sustained high-throughput workload — can you give a headroom estimate?
[20:55] Alyssa: We'll include a pricing sketch based on expected QPS and model choices in the follow-up email. For long-running commitments, Dedicated reserved pricing is the best lever.
[21:20] Tomás: Can we get a list of tests you'll run in the benchmark?
[21:34] Marcus: Yes — latency, throughput, p50/p95/p99, error rate, output regression against golden prompts, and cost-per-request. We'll populate the spreadsheet and share.
[22:00] [22:00] Small wrap-up chatter; scheduling follow-up for week of 2025-05-26.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors (e.g., function names split, minor mis-hear of 'KV cache' as 'K-V cash'), filler words, and some speaker attribution rounds labeled generically.

End of transcript.
